quotes.text: Permissions are living data. Treating them like a static list means you're always in the past, never in the live state of your environment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes permission reviews as a continuous data problem.

quotes.text: The solution isn't throwing more people at the review. It's building a way to query and consolidate this data automatically, so the moment something changes, your reports reflect that.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core recommendation to automate auditing.

quotes.text: Where it gets messy is that inheritance is invisible if you only look at direct permissions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights the most common blind spot in permission audits.

quotes.text: Keeping that history means you can prove the audit ran at a given time and see exactly what happened if it didn't finish. For compliance, that audit trail can be as valuable as the permission report itself.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why job logs matter for compliance evidence.

quotes.text: At enterprise scale, guessing at permissions isn't an option. Without a live, accurate view, you're hoping nothing slips through and hope isn't a security strategy.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A strong closing argument for continuous permission monitoring.

chapters.title: Why traditional permission reviews break at enterprise scale
Building the foundation with PnP PowerShell
Mining permission data with Microsoft Graph API
Automating the audit with Azure Automation

takeaways: Manual, spreadsheet-based SharePoint permission reviews cannot keep up with thousands of changing sites, inheritance and nested groups.
PnP PowerShell with certificate-based app-only authentication and Microsoft Graph lets you enumerate every site and resolve effective permissions down to users and guests.
Azure Automation runbooks with Key Vault secrets turn the audit into a scheduled, logged process that can alert on risky changes such as new guests.
hook: Your SharePoint permission reviews are outdated the moment they are finished, and guests hide in nested groups no one checks. This episode is for SharePoint and Microsoft 365 admins responsible for access governance in large tenants. Learn how to combine PnP PowerShell, Microsoft Graph and Azure Automation into a tenant-wide, automated permission audit.
